findings.recommendation: Space the attempts with exponential backoff and jitter (e.g. 1s, 4s, 16s…), ideally from a persisted retry queue rather than an in-process loop. Today a merchant endpoint that answers 503 during a few-second restart receives five requests within milliseconds, all fail, and the event is dropped: the "retried, up to five attempts" promise of the proposal buys no resilience, and a struggling merchant is hammered instead of given time to recover. While there, do not retry non-retryable answers (4xx other than 408/429): they fail identically five times.
findings.title: Webhook retries fire back-to-back with no backoff

findings.evidence:
console.debug(`webhook ${event.id} dropped after ${MAX_ATTEMPTS} attempts`);
return false;
findings.recommendation: When a merchant endpoint keeps failing, the payment notification is lost and the only trace is a free-text `console.debug` line, which production log levels usually discard; a non-2xx response is not logged at all, so its status code never appears, and the `false` returned by `deliver` is ignored by the listener. Use the project's structured `logger` (src/logger.ts): log each failed attempt at warn with fields (eventId, merchant/payment id, attempt, HTTP status or error), log the final drop at error, and emit a metric/counter for delivered vs dropped webhooks so an alert can fire. Never log the full webhook URL if it may embed a merchant secret.
findings.title: A dropped webhook is invisible to operators

findings.recommendation: `publish` in src/events.ts awaits each listener in turn, so a merchant endpoint that times out holds the payment service's `publish` call for 5 attempts × 5 s = 25 s, and delays every later listener. Whether the payment service awaits `publish` on its request path was not verified. Hand delivery off to a background queue/worker (which also gives R-ops-1 its backoff) instead of awaiting it inside the listener.
findings.title: Webhook delivery blocks the payment event publisher for up to 25 s
